ai.description: *Liurana indica* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum. It is distinguished by a prominent, fleshy papilla on the tongue and distinct, enlarged digital discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Liurana indica* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, fleshy papilla on the center of its tongue, a unique feature absent in other similar Indian frogs.
ai.habitat: *Liurana indica* inhabits high-altitude, moss-covered rocky streams and moist leaf litter within temperate evergreen forests of the Eastern Himalayas, typically above 2,000m.
ai.behavior: The Indian Papilla-tongued Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects among leaf litter and damp forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Liurana indica* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in damp soil or moss near streams, exhibiting direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Liurana indica* is endemic to the high-altitude regions of the Eastern Himalayas in Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Liurana indica* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard emanating from mossy rocks near mountain streams.
